title: Exodus Bible Quiz - Chapter 22
description: Ten questions on Exodus 22: the laws about theft, damage, borrowed goods, the poor and the stranger.

questions.text: If a man steals an ox and kills or sells it, how much must he pay?
questions.explanation: He shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

questions.text: If the stolen animal is found alive in the thief's hand, what must he pay?
questions.explanation: If the stolen ox, donkey or sheep is found in his hand alive, he shall pay double.

questions.text: If a fire spreads through thorns and burns another man's grain, who must make restitution?
questions.explanation: He who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.

answers.text: The one who kindled the fire

questions.text: What should a keeper do if an animal left with him is torn in pieces?
questions.explanation: If it is torn in pieces, he shall bring it for evidence, and he shall not make good what was torn.

answers.text: Pay its full price to the owner
Bring a sin offering to the altar
Give the owner one of his own animals
Bring it as evidence; no payment is due

questions.text: Whom shall you not allow to live?
questions.explanation: The law says: 'You shall not allow a sorceress to live.'

questions.text: Why must Israel not wrong or oppress an alien?
questions.explanation: You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, 'for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.'

answers.text: Aliens bring trade to the land
Aliens pay tribute to the king
They were aliens in the land of Egypt

questions.text: What may you not do when you lend money to a poor person among God's people?
questions.explanation: You shall not be to him as a creditor; you shall not charge him interest.

answers.text: Lend to him on the Sabbath
Lend him silver instead of grain

questions.text: When must a neighbor's garment taken as collateral be given back?
questions.explanation: You shall restore it to him before the sun goes down, for it is his only covering.

answers.text: At the end of the year

questions.text: Besides God, whom shall you not curse?
questions.explanation: The law says: 'You shall not blaspheme God, nor curse a ruler of your people.'

questions.text: On which day was the firstborn of cattle and sheep to be given to God?
questions.explanation: It was to be with its mother seven days, and on the eighth day given to God.
